files.role: Cache-entry LCE1 envelope parser/writer, explicit hit/miss reasons, serializable-type trait and allocation-free type-erased codec descriptor with function-pointer adapters.
files.limits: The source calls the outer envelope stabilized/stability-critical while the CacheCodecImpl format documentation explicitly remains experimental. This file alone does not resolve a released stable-format guarantee; repository compatibility rules take precedence over speculative preservation of intermediate unstable builds. Exact wrapper behavior is established, but concrete production body codecs, backend Miss handling and lance_arrow IPC implementation remain pending. No tests executed or external specifications fetched. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:22-36; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:51-60; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:191-228; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:317-370)
ranges: SPDX/module docs describe concrete CacheCodecImpl -> type-erased CacheCodec. The declared envelope is LCE1 magic4, envelope_version u8, type-id byte length LEu16 plus UTF-8, body-version LEu32, then body. Hand framing is called stability-critical/unchanging, while bodies use protobuf headers by convention. Parse/identity/version/body Result failures become cache misses; historical shape self-healing is current documentation, not a mandate to add old-unstable migrations.

Imports Write,Arc,Bytes,core Error/Result and sibling entry IO. Public MAGIC=[L,C,E,1] with hex4C434531. Comments claim this avoids earlier small-length/tag shapes, but no arbitrary-payload collision proof or released-fixture verification is present. Public exposure allows backends to inspect prefixes.

has_cache_envelope checks only first4 bytes equal MAGIC using get; returns false for length<4 and true for exactly4 magic bytes even though no complete envelope exists. Private ENVELOPE_VERSION=u8=1 is the only accepted outer version.

Private ParsedEnvelope borrows type_id and owns type_version/body_offset. parse_envelope starts offset0, safely gets4 magic bytes then version byte; mismatch/truncation returns None. Offset additions here are bounded small constants. No allocation, IO, logging or error object is made by the parser itself.

Parser gets LEu16 id byte length, borrows that many bytes, validates UTF-8, then reads LEu32 body version. Returns body_offset=11+id_byte_length, bounded at65546 by u16 length. Empty/NUL-containing type IDs and version0 are accepted. It does not check body availability/content, trailing bytes, checksum, type identity or version support; The wrapper checks exact type identity and rejects body versions newer than its current version; older/equal body-version handling is delegated to the body decoder. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:330-361)

write_envelope first checks UTF-8 byte length fitsu16, otherwise Error::io includes actual length and65535 limit with no writes yet. It then write_all's magic/version/length/id/body-version in order and returns11+id.len(). IO failures propagate and can leave a partial envelope; there is no rollback, buffering, flush or checksum.

Section separator and public Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq CacheMissReason enumerate InvalidEnvelope (bad/unknown/truncated/non-UTF8 framing), TypeMismatch, VersionTooNew and BodyError. Docs assign all reasons recomputation by the backend and allow distinct metrics; this enum itself neither evicts nor invokes a loader.
Public Debug CacheDecode<T> is Hit(T) or Miss(CacheMissReason). Consuming hit() returns Some(value) or None, discarding any reason. There is no Result error channel or automatic retry in this helper.

CacheCodecImpl documentation explicitly marks serialized format experimental/no stability guarantee between releases, then describes future append-only TYPE_ID/protobuf field/enum rules and version bumps. Separate TYPE_ID docs below say must not change once shipped. Record this tension rather than inferring a released guarantee. Body serialization order and version-aware matching read order are implementor obligations; wrapper owns envelope only.

Public CacheCodecImpl:Send+Sync requires TYPE_ID:static str, CURRENT_VERSION:u32, serialize(&self,&mut CacheEntryWriter)->Result<()> and deserialize(&mut CacheEntryReader)->Result<Self> where Self:Sized. Constants and deserialize return make this a concrete implementation trait, not the erased backend object. It does not require Any,DeepSizeOf or Debug; from_impl later adds static lifetime. No mandated protobuf header is type-enforced.

pub(crate) ArcAny aliases Arc<dyn Any+Send+Sync>. Public Copy/Clone CacheCodec contains static type id,u32 version and two plain function pointers for erased-body write/read. Descriptor construction itself allocates no heap state; function-pointer execution can allocate or fail. Private fields prevent outside direct mutation.
Custom Debug prints CacheCodec with type_id and version and finish_non_exhaustive, omitting function-pointer fields. It does not serialize bytes or invoke codecs.

serialize_via_impl<T:CacheCodecImpl+static> downcast_ref expects exact concrete T and panics with cache-layer-bug message if wrong, then calls T::serialize. deserialize_via_impl delegates T::deserialize with ?, allocates Arc<T> on success and erases it. Panic/allocation failures are not caught here.

Public CacheCodec::new accepts explicit static type id,u32 version and write/read function pointers, supporting orphan-rule custom adapters. It simply stores fields without checking identity uniqueness/nonemptiness/id length, version range, concrete type coherence, or roundtrip compatibility. Length validation happens when writing envelope.

from_impl<T> copies associated TYPE_ID/CURRENT_VERSION and monomorphized adapter pointers. Const type_id(&self) returns static identity for backend routing. No public version accessor appears in this implementation; readers get stored input version from CacheEntryReader.

serialize writes the full envelope first, constructs CacheEntryWriter::with_pos at body offset, then calls erased serializer directly. A body error or adapter wrong-type panic can leave envelope/partial body in the underlying writer. No temporary full-entry buffer or transactional write is provided by this wrapper.

deserialize returns CacheDecode<ArcAny>; parser failure logs debug and returns InvalidEnvelope, then exact type-id mismatch logs actual/expected and returns TypeMismatch. Order matters: malformed framing is rejected before identity, and identity before body-version gate. The never fails doc concerns Result parse failures, not a panic-catching guarantee.

If input body version>codec version, logs and returns VersionTooNew without calling body decoder. Older/equal values, including0, are passed to implementation; there is no minimum supported version registry or backward migration here. Wrapper numeric ordering alone does not prove body can read every older version.

Constructs reader over original whole Bytes at envelope.body_offset with input type_version. Decoder Ok is Hit without checking reader consumed all bytes; Err logs full Display and becomes BodyError with original detailed error discarded from outcome. Panics are not caught and custom callbacks can perform arbitrary effects despite local in-memory parsing. No checksum/authentication or postdecode concrete-type validation is present.

cfg(test) Widget stores n:u32, uses TYPE_ID=test.Widget/v1. Its body writes a raw length-prefixed four-byte LE n, with no protobuf header; decoder reads raw then requires exactly4 payload bytes, otherwise Error::io bad widget. This demonstrates body primitive choice is implementor-defined.

serialize_widget makes fresh Arc Widget, serializes into Vec and converts Bytes, unwrapping errors. miss_reason converts Hit to None/Miss to reason. deserialize_widget uses wrapper then downcasts and try_unwrap's Arc, assuming test codec returns sole-owned Widget. These are private test helpers with no production panic guarantee.

Roundtrip test asserts LCE1 prefix and DEADBEEF Widget equality; magic helper test includes valid bytes, exactly MAGIC alone(true), short LCE,false foreign/empty. It explicitly separates prefix recognition from full envelope validation.

Wrong-first-byte fixture expects InvalidEnvelope. Historical-shape test synthesizes LEu64 length42 plus42 zeros, and a small tag-byte vector, both misses. These are in-source synthetic cases, not checked-in released fixtures or implemented legacy decoders.

Unknown envelope byteFF returns InvalidEnvelope. Manually framed some.OtherType plus otherwise plausible raw widget body returns TypeMismatch. Tests do not verify combined-invalid precedence beyond these one-cause fixtures.

CURRENT_VERSION+1 with matching type/raw body yields VersionTooNew. Truncation test cuts valid entry at0,1,4,5,7,9 and expects InvalidEnvelope; it samples positions rather than every envelope boundary and does not cover invalid UTF-8 id.

One-byte raw Widget payload under valid envelope yields BodyError. reader_exposes_envelope_version writes body-version7 and constructs CacheEntryReader directly at recorded offset, confirming version7/raw value5; it bypasses CacheCodec's version1 gate and does not prove wrapper reads future versions. No tests here cover writer failures/overlong id, older-version branching, trailing-byte acceptance, wrong-type serialize panic or custom decoder panic.

files.role: In-memory dataset manifest, metadata transformations, fragment accounting, protobuf conversion, writer/version descriptors and frozen V1 self-describing reader adapter. Selected public types/functions are reexported by format; ManifestSummary and VersionPart are public inside the private child but not reexported.
ranges: SPDX/imports connect async_trait, Bytes, chrono, DeepSizeOf, file schema adapters/exact versions and V1 dictionaries/reader, IO ProtoStruct/Reader/read_struct, Path, prost/Timestamp, maps/ranges/Arc, Fragment/interner/row IDs, feature bits, LanceCache/Schema/errors and ObjectStore/Registry. Lance-file parsing is now analyzed; full backend IO remains pending.

Manifest derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/DeepSizeOf. Public fields hold schema, dataset version/branch, optional writer version, Arc<Vec<Fragment>>, aux/index/transaction positions, u128 nanosecond timestamp, tag, reader/writer words, optional u32 max-fragment high-water mark, optional transaction path, next_row_id:u64, exact DataStorageFormat, config/table_metadata/base_paths maps. Only fragment_offsets:Vec<usize> is private. Docs require fragments sorted by ID with gaps, but constructors/conversion below do not sort or enforce this; public fragments replacement can stale the private offsets. Dataset version, writer-library version and data-file version are separate values.

DETACHED_VERSION_MASK is bit63 (0x8000000000000000); is_detached_version tests it only. compute_fragment_offsets maps each Fragment::num_rows().unwrap_or_default(), chains final zero, and scans prefix sums into N+1 entries, including terminal total (empty list->[0]). Unknown row count contributes zero; ordinary usize addition is unchecked. It preserves fragment order and performs no row-ID mapping.

Default ManifestSummary has seven u64 counters. Consuming conversion to BTreeMap<String,String> writes exactly total_fragments, total_data_files, total_files_size, total_deletion_files, total_data_file_rows, total_deletion_file_rows, total_rows, all decimal strings. Type is pub in private module, not facade-reexported, though callers can infer the summary return type and use its public fields.

Manifest::new accepts owned Schema, shared fragment Vec, storage format and base-path map; computes offsets, starts version1/current WriterVersion, zero timestamp/feature words/aux position/next row ID, absent branch/tag/index/transaction/high-water mark, and empty config/table metadata. It does not inspect formats, assign fragment IDs, validate schema/carriers or perform IO.

new_from_previous uses supplied schema/fragments and recomputed offsets; increments previous version with unchecked +1, retains branch/high-water/next row ID/storage/config/table metadata/bases and refreshes writer version. It clears aux/index/time/tag/transaction references and preserves only STICKY_PAIRED_FLAGS separately in reader/writer words. It neither normalizes nor validates half-set pairs and does not preserve covered-index bit here. Caller must restore index metadata as comment states.

shallow_clone is in-memory: clones each Fragment, stamps ref_base_id only on base and overlay DataFiles whose base_id is None via referenced_lance_files_mut, and similarly stamps local deletion descriptor. Existing external base IDs remain. Inline/column metadata remains cloned; no files are opened/copied.

Shallow clone keeps source version/writer/aux position/time/high-water/offsets/next row ID/storage/config/table metadata, uses new branch and transaction_file=Some(input), clears tag/index/transaction_section, and allocates a new fragment Arc. It masks each feature word to covered-index bit OR sticky pairs, preserving each side independently. Source comments justify conservative covered-index retention; index metadata copy happens outside this function. Base map is cloned and insert(ref_base_id, BasePath(...,is_dataset_root=true)) can replace an existing entry without collision validation.

timestamp splits u128 nanos into remainder<1e9 and casts whole seconds to i64, uses chrono from_timestamp with unwrap_or_default fallback for unrepresentable date, then Utc. No error returned. set_timestamp actually accepts u128 raw nanos despite DateTime doc wording. config_mut/table_metadata_mut/schema_metadata_mut return mutable maps with no validation, persistence or feature recomputation.

field_metadata_mut delegates recursive schema field_by_id_mut then yields metadata or None. Deprecated update_config extends config with key overwrite semantics; deprecated delete_config_keys retains entries whose names are absent from supplied slice. No table configuration semantics are checked.

Deprecated replace_schema_metadata replaces whole schema map. Deprecated replace_field_metadata replaces selected field map and returns Ok, or InvalidInput with field ID if missing. The preceding no-op comment is inconsistent with the implemented error branch; document the error as behavior. No primary-key validation is invoked.

detach_sparse_inline_row_ids sums visible lengths of Inline row-ID payloads (not deduplicated, not created/updated versions). Returns unchanged if sum==0 or sum.saturating_mul(4)>=buffer_len, preserving exact quarter boundary. Otherwise Arc::make_mut obtains fragments and each Inline gets Bytes::copy_from_slice wrapped in a fresh InlineRowIds (new digest memo); other metadata unchanged. A shared fragments Arc triggers clone-on-write. Caller-provided buffer_len is trusted; whole original buffer release is not guaranteed while other owners/slices survive. Ordinary sum can overflow; multiplication is saturating.

update_max_fragment_id returns for empty fragments, otherwise takes maximum u64 ID then try_into u32 and unwraps (panic above u32::MAX). It initializes absent mark or raises it only, retaining historic high water after deletes. No Result or ID validation; a stored larger mark is preserved.

max_fragment_id returns stored u32 mark widened to u64 if present, otherwise computes maximum existing fragment ID, with None only for unset+empty. max_field_id compares schema max (default-1) with every field ID in base and overlay referenced files (default-1); includes dropped schema fields and does not explicitly filter tombstone or reserved IDs. No field IDs are assigned.

fragments_since rejects since.version>=self.version, including equality, with InvalidInput describing newer version. It uses since.max_fragment_id as threshold and clones current fragments with strictly greater IDs, or all if absent. This is an ID-high-water heuristic, not content comparison; docs exclude recycling and it does not validate common lineage/branch.

fragments_by_offset_range uses logical row offsets, not row IDs: binary_search start in cached N+1 prefix offsets, otherwise insertion index minus1, then walk fragment indices. Break when fragment start>=end OR fragment end<=start; append(start,&Fragment) otherwise. Unknown current length acts as zero. It does not validate/recompute offsets, sort, deduplicate equal offsets or explicitly validate empty/reversed ranges. Duplicated offsets/zero-length fragments may select a zero-length entry and break before later data; callers need valid coherent counts. Returned elements borrow fragments, despite doc return wording showing owned Fragment.

uses_stable_row_ids checks reader word FLAG_STABLE_ROW_IDS only, not per-fragment metadata or writer word. serialized builds pb::Manifest then encode_to_vec: raw protobuf bytes suitable for IPC/temp storage, not a complete on-disk manifest with footer/sections/dictionaries.

summary folds fragments: total_data_files counts base f.files only and total_files_size sums only known sizes of those base files, excluding overlays/deletion/index files despite broad docs. total_rows sums only known f.num_rows; deletion_file presence counts even if deleted count unknown, known deletion counts sum separately. total_fragments is Vec length; total_data_file_rows=total_rows+total_deletion_file_rows, not sum of all physical counts when some lengths unknown. Ordinary u64 additions are unchecked; no IO resolves missing sizes/counts.

Async populate_manifest_schema_dictionaries is a V1 compatibility adapter. Exact V1 delegates populate_schema_dictionaries(&mut schema,reader).await; V2_0/V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 are explicit no-ops. No version selector or writer-library comparison is used. Included doctest wraps an async Result function, not ignore; it was not compiled.

BasePath stores public id:u32, optional name, is_dataset_root:bool and full URI/path String. new assigns without URI/ID validation; extract_path synchronously delegates ObjectStore::extract_path_from_uri(registry,&path), propagating Result. Actual parsing/registry behavior is pending; no store initialization in this body.

BasePath custom DeepSizeOf children adds name children + twice path children + size_of<bool>(). This literally overcounts path allocation relative to normal one-string ownership and adds inline bool as a child; source gives no rationale. It is an estimator, not measured retained heap.

WriterVersion stores public library/version Strings plus optional prerelease/build metadata. DataStorageFormat stores public file_format:String and ConcreteFileVersion; new uses literal lance, getter returns exact enum, Default uses stable_file_version() resolved elsewhere. TryFrom protobuf preserves file_format without checking it equals lance and parses version via from_manifest_string. Exact mappings are now covered at rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27 and rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-261; selector acceptance remains distinct from persisted strings.

ManifestBuildConfig is a data-only public Debug/Clone struct with auto_set_feature_flags, resolved timestamp_nanos, use_stable_row_ids, optional legacy mode/storage_format, disable_transaction_file, migration_next_row_id and Arc<SpilledRowLineage>. Docs specify sticky row IDs, overwrite-only storage override precedence, migration bypass and prefetched spilled sequences needed for rewrite/update; no enforcement/default implementation occurs in this file. Clock resolution deliberately belongs to caller; cfg(test) clock mocking in lance is a source comment, consumer implementation pending.

VersionPart Major/Minor/Patch is pub in private module with no facade reexport. Private bump_version increments chosen semver u64 component, resets lower components for major/minor, leaves prerelease/build intact and uses ordinary unchecked additions.

Private split_version parses semver, returns None on error, extracts nonempty pre/build as optional Strings, clears both in parsed object and returns clean major.minor.patch plus separate components. Docs include rc/build/invalid examples. No library check here.

Deprecated semver is a distinct lenient parser: split self.version at first dash, parse first three dot-separated components as u32 with missing minor/patch default0, return remainder after dash as optional borrowed tag. Extra dot parts are ignored, explicit prerelease/build fields and library are ignored; plus-build in patch can cause parse failure. It is not equivalent to full semver::Version parsing despite doc wording.

lance_lib_version rejects library != exact lowercase lance, parses self.version with semver, then when separate prerelease/build fields are Some parses and overwrites corresponding parsed components. None leaves components embedded in version string intact. Any parse error returns None. Arbitrary nonsemver WriterVersion values remain constructible; only this interpretation fails.

Deprecated semver_or_panic wraps old parser and panics with raw version on failure. older_than uses lance_lib_version().expect then compares against release major/minor/patch with empty pre/build, so prerelease ordering follows semver. Deprecated bump expects valid Lance version, increments numeric part, clears only prerelease if keep_tag=false (build retained), splits back to clean fields and clones library. Non-Lance/invalid versions panic; future-private wording is intent, not current restriction.

WriterVersion Default outside cfg(test) parses compile-time CARGO_PKG_VERSION and emits library lance, clean version and separate pre/build, panicking if invalid. Under this crate cfg(test), same fields then bump(Patch,true), retaining pre/build but using next patch. Dependency builds do not automatically inherit cfg(test); no actual Cargo version value is asserted here.

ProtoStruct maps Manifest::Proto=pb::Manifest. BasePath From conversions copy/move matching id/name/root/path fields, no URI/duplicate validation. Converting owned BasePath to protobuf consumes Strings.

Manifest TryFrom starts timestamp conversion by casting signed seconds/nanos to u128 then sec*1e9+nanos; absent timestamp defaults later to0. Negative or out-of-range values are not validated and casts/arithmetic can wrap/panic according to overflow policy. Any Some writer_version message becomes Some even with empty library/version; the fully-set comment does not enforce nonempty fields.

A fresh DataFileFieldInterner converts all protobuf fragments, sharing repeated base field/column lists and inline version bytes across this manifest, preserving fragment order. It computes logical offsets and wraps fields/schema metadata. If reader stable-row bit is set but any fragment lacks row_id_meta, returns Internal All fragments must have row ids; empty fragment set passes. It does not decode inline sequences or validate Column carriers.

If data_format absent, infer exact version from all base/overlay files, rejecting mixed versions; with no files use stable_file_version when deprecated writer bit2 set, else V1. If data_format present, trust converted DataStorageFormat without comparing per-file versions. Then convert schema via FieldsWithMeta. This conversion alone does not invoke ensure_can_read_manifest/paired flag checks or reject fragment_tree.

Final Manifest retains raw version/branch/flags/high-water/next row/config/table metadata, casts aux/index/transaction offsets to usize without checked conversion, normalizes empty tag/transaction_file to None, and collects base-path entries by id into HashMap (later duplicate ID replaces earlier). Uses converted fragments/schema/format and computed offsets. Unknown/ignored protobuf fields including fragment_tree have no Rust representation here.

Manifest->protobuf omits timestamp if nanos==0, else divides into seconds cast i64 and subsecond i32 without overflow validation. Converts schema through FieldsWithMeta and separately encodes schema metadata String values as UTF8 Vec; clones branch/writer strings including separate pre/build and converts fragments in order. This conversion does not validate inputs.

Output sets fragment_tree=None, preserves metadata/flags/high-water/counts, casts usize positions to u64, writes absent tag/transaction file as empty String, always includes data_format with exact to_manifest_string, clones config and emits base_paths from HashMap values in unspecified order. transaction_section presence retained. This is a protobuf object conversion, not atomic manifest publication or canonical byte ordering.

Public async_trait SelfDescribingFileReader offers default try_new_self_described(ObjectStore,Path,optional&LanceCache): await store.open, convert reader into Arc then delegate required try_new_self_described_from_reader. Both require Self:Sized; from_reader accepts Arc<dyn Reader>. Docs prefer fragment readers for cached schemas; no caching algorithm or format detection is implemented by the trait default.

Only implementation here is V1FileReader: read_metadata(reader,cache), require metadata.manifest_position or Internal with reader path, read_struct<Manifest> at position, hydrate V1 dictionaries, take schema/max_field_id(default0), then call V1 try_new_from_reader with path, reader clone, Some(metadata), schema, numeric0,0,max ID and cache. Errors propagate at awaits; compatibility adapter does not add a V2 self-describing implementation. The numeric arguments are fragment_id=0, field_id_offset=0 and schema max_field_id. Complete V1 reader construction/cache/metadata behavior is now covered (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:165-294); backend IO remains pending.

cfg(test) imports feature bit, overlay/data/deletion types, Arrow/core fields and bitmap. Shallow clone fixture with one base and one overlay asserts both local base IDs become7. It does not assert existing external IDs, deletion stamping, feature retention, URI behavior or disk clone.

Old empty manifest fixture with absent data_format recovers V1 without deprecated writer bit, current stable with it. Persistence rejection loops stable,next,legacy,0.3 and asserts conversion error. These are constructed protobuf values, not released historical fixtures or proof all version aliases are covered.

Canonical output fixture asserts V2_0 serializes version string2.0. Missing-format fixture recovers exact V2_0 from a file even when prior in-memory storage field was V1, then rejects V2_0/V2_1 files when protobuf format is removed. Explicit-format mixed-version validation is not tested here.

Detach fixture holds two10-byte slices of one64-byte buffer, supplies logical buffer_len80 then81. Exact quarter retains original pointers; below quarter copies both pointers outside original allocation and verifies second payload contents. It trusts the provided length, does not assert deallocation/RSS, Arc sharing or digest behavior.

Writer default fixture asserts lance, three-part clean version, cargo prerelease tag, no build metadata for this package, reconstructed Cargo major/minor and patch+1 under cfg(test), and each numeric bump produces greater version. expected_tag is split from Cargo text; fixture assumes package metadata layout, not a general parser proof.
Split-version test covers release, rc.1, rc.1+build.123, build-only and invalid string, with exact clean/pre/build components. Does not cover the deprecated lenient parser.

Writer tests compare rc.1<release, reconstruct rc.1+build.123 and all numeric/pre/build fields, and allow nonsemver WriterVersion custom-build-v1 while lance_lib_version returns None. No other-library or invalid separate-component fixture.
Deprecated older_than fixture requires rc2.0.0 below2.0.0/2.0.1 but not1.9.9, release2.0.0 not older than itself but older than2.0.1. Panic behavior for invalid/non-Lance input is not tested.

Offset-range fixture has three fragments of10/15/20 rows, expects0..10 first only,5..15 first two,15..50 latter two at offsets10/25;45..100 and200..400 empty. It does not cover zero/unknown counts, reversed/empty interior ranges or stale offsets.

Max-field fixture uses schema IDs0/2, multiple files/fragments including dropped ID43 and expects43. Tests dropped physical IDs beyond schema maximum without reading data or assigning IDs through Manifest.
Overlay max-field fixture puts ID43 only in overlay over base0 and expects43, proving referenced overlay IDs participate in high-water calculation. No tombstone/reserved-ID boundary case.

Config fixture constructs three-fragment manifest, extends config_mut with two keys and removes one; equality confirms in-memory map mutation. It does not recompute feature flags, persist metadata or test deprecated APIs.

Summary test starts empty manifest (all seven zero), two known-zero fragments (two files/fragments but zero rows/sizes), then three in-memory fragments100/250/75 (425 rows, three files, unknown sizes contribute0). Comments saying write files do not correspond to IO in this test.

Summary deletion fixture sets one known1000-byte file/50 physical rows/10 deleted, expects40 live,50 total-data rows,10 deleted and one deletion/file/fragment, then seven string-map entries. Overlay omission and unknown physical/deleted-count combinations are not tested. All file tests/doctest were read, not executed.
files.limits: All1825 lines read in bounded chunks. Visibility facade: rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:21-25. Local metadata conversion, counters and helpers are covered; transaction builder enforcement, commit flags/support checks, IO framing, full RowIdSequence and dataset consumers remain pending; nested wire codecs are now covered at rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:1-884. Exact file-version, overlay and row-version implementations are now covered in their own L2 entries. No build/test/benchmark, file-format release qualification or external-dependency behavior verification was performed.

files.role: Physical DataBlock representations, Arrow normalization and validated reconstruction, shared statistics, range builders, dictionary/null conversion and regression tests.
files.limits: All2898 lines freshly read in ANALYZE79. Source deductions only: no repository build, test, lint, benchmark, generator, installation or network. Public fields and infallible helpers retain caller preconditions. Full structural/legacy primitive callers remain pending.
ranges: License and module docs place DataBlock between Arrow ArrayData and typed arrays: physical representations can combine logical types and expose codec-oriented buffers. Docs require variable offsets to start at zero; Arrow conversion validation actually permits a bounded nonzero first offset. Public fields do not enforce this invariant.

Imports connect Arrow arrays/dictionary keys, buffer builders, checked ArrayData construction, datatype byte widths, LanceBuffer, errors and statistics. No asynchronous work or IO is implemented here. Arc/RwLock protect the shared statistics map, not mutable physical data.

Public AllNullDataBlock contains only num_values. Arrow conversion creates a null array of the requested type with count cast to usize; validate is ignored. Serialization has no buffers. A comment plans deprecation in2.1 but the type has no deprecated attribute and remains dispatched.

Public BlockInfo tuple exposes Arc<RwLock<HashMap<Stat,Arc<dyn Array>>>>. Default/new allocate an empty map. Clones share the map and statistic arrays. PartialEq acquires both read locks and compares entries, unwrapping poison errors. It does not compare Arc identity. Cache validity is not tied to buffer mutation.

Public NullableDataBlock contains boxed child, packed validity bytes and shared stats. Arrow conversion always converts child with validation enabled, attaches validity and performs checked build. Serialized validity precedes child buffers; data_size adds visible validity bytes. Legacy-deprecation comment is future intent, not an attribute or removed implementation.

Public ConstantDataBlock stores one scalar byte sequence and logical count. into_buffers emits one scalar buffer and data_size measures only that buffer, not expanded values. Arrow conversion is todo and panics. try_clone returns Ok with a cheap buffer clone and copied count.

Public FixedWidthDataBlock exposes data, bits_per_value, num_values and BlockInfo. do_into_arrow repacks bits_per_value8 into packed Boolean bits by taking at most declared count bytes and treating nonzero as true; otherwise moves the buffer directly. Checked Arrow construction uses requested datatype/count/null_count0, but no independent physical-width versus requested-type equality check except the Boolean branch.

FixedWidth public into_arrow ignores the caller validation flag and always uses checked construction. Serialization returns one buffer; try_clone copies metadata and shares buffer/statistics ownership; data_size reports visible byte length. This is not retained allocation size.

Private generic VariableWidthDataBlockBuilder stores offsets Vec<T> initially[0] and byte Vec with estimated capacity cast to usize. Offset type is chosen when the first input establishes builder shape.

Variable builder validate_append unwraps VariableWidth and validates selected offsets. append_validated assumes that proof, debug-checks width and borrows typed offsets. It computes selected byte span and checked-adds its length to current data; arithmetic overflow or inability to represent new total in T returns NotSupported before mutation.

After size checks, variable builder copies the selected payload and appends rebased offsets after the selection start. Finish derives count from offsets.len()-1 and emits owned buffers with fresh empty stats. Selected-range validation need not inspect offsets outside that range; this builder does not validate UTF-8.

Private BitmapDataBlockBuilder reserves estimated_bytes*8 bits, with unchecked multiplication. Validation is a no-op; append unwraps FixedWidth and appends selected packed bits without an explicit bits_per_value check or declared-count bound. Finish creates bits_per_value1 with builder logical length and fresh stats.

Private FixedWidthDataBlockBuilder asserts a multiple-of-eight width, stores bytes_per_value and reserves estimated bytes. Validation is a no-op. Append asserts matching bit width, multiplies cast range endpoints by byte width and slices bytes; malformed ranges can panic. Zero bits pass construction but finish divides by zero. Finish count derives from appended byte length.

Private StructDataBlockBuilder stores child builders. Validation indexes input children for each builder and validates all before appending. Too few children panic; extra children are ignored. Child appends occur sequentially, so a later append error can leave prior children changed. Finish always sets parent validity None and creates empty stats, discarding input parent validity.

Private default AllNullDataBlockBuilder counts selected rows with ordinary subtraction/addition. Validation ignores both block and selection; append does not inspect type or bounds. Finish returns an AllNull block.

Public FixedSizeListBlock exposes child and dimension. num_values divides child count by dimension, truncating remainders and panicking for zero. try_into_flat rejects Nullable children with None, recursively multiplies physical width and divides logical count for nested/fixed children, retains leaf stats, and panics for other child kinds.

flatten_as_fixed takes mutable self but only recursively clones the fixed leaf: it does not multiply dimensions or update counts. from_flat recursively follows Arrow FixedSizeList dimensions, divides width and multiplies count with ordinary arithmetic and no dimension validation. Other requested types simply return FixedWidth. Retained shared statistics are not recomputed.

FixedSizeList Arrow conversion computes count using its own dimension, expects a FixedSizeList datatype or panics, converts child with validation and checked-builds the requested Arrow layout. There is no explicit equality check between stored and schema dimensions. Buffers and size are inherited from the child.

Private FixedSizeListBlockBuilder stores child builder and first-input dimension. Both validation and append unwrap incoming FSL and multiply selected row endpoints by stored dimension without checked arithmetic or an incoming-dimension equality check. Finish wraps the child result.

Private NullableDataBlockBuilder reserves a validity builder and delegates validation only to its inner child. Append changes the child first, then constructs a BooleanBuffer over selected raw validity bits and appends it. Malformed validity can therefore panic after child mutation. Finish wraps child and packed validity with new empty stats.

Public OpaqueBlock contains a vector of buffers, logical count and stats. It represents encoded data that cannot yet be turned into Arrow. data_size sums visible buffer lengths, with no capacity accounting or shared-buffer deduplication.

Public VariableWidthBlock exposes data, offsets, bits_per_offset, num_values and stats. Docs prescribe num_values+1 offsets starting at0. Private unit ValidVariableWidthLayout is passed only after local validation to permit unchecked construction; it has no fields or lifetime tying it to a particular instance. Correct private call ordering is part of the safety argument.

append_error produces CorruptFile with pseudo filename variable width data block, selected range, count, offset width and both buffer sizes. validate_offsets_for_append<T> checks width matches T, whole offset-buffer divisibility and ordered selection bounded by num_values, with checked usize endpoint conversions.

Append validation borrows the typed whole offset buffer, requires a present end offset, then checks only the selected inclusive offsets for monotonicity, nonnegativity and payload bounds. It permits nonzero first offsets, does not require the complete logical offset count and does not inspect UTF-8. Whole-buffer divisibility can reject padding accepted by Arrow conversion.

VariableWidth into_arrow ignores validate. Binary/Utf8 require32-bit offsets; LargeBinary/LargeUtf8 require64. Width mismatch is CorruptFile even when count is zero. Unsupported requested types use a checked Arrow fallback; empty supported arrays also use checked fallback. Nonempty supported arrays validate then use the private unchecked builder.

expected_offset_bits maps only four classic binary/string types. layout_error and format_layout_error include requested datatype, declared count, width and buffer sizes in CorruptFile diagnostics. Other requested types are left to Arrow checked validation.

validate_layout computes required (count+1)*offset_bytes using checked arithmetic, requires sufficient offset bytes and dispatches i32/i64 or reports unsupported width. UTF-8 validation is enabled for string types. Extra offset bytes are accepted; the caller already checked datatype/width consistency.

validate_offsets_and_values slices exactly the required offset prefix before typed borrowing, so non-width-aligned trailing padding is ignored. It validates monotonicity and payload bounds. Strings validate the selected payload from first through final offset as UTF-8 once, then require every offset to be a character boundary, rescanning to report the first bad boundary. Unused payload prefix/suffix need not be valid UTF-8. A nonzero first offset and unused suffix are allowed.

offset_violation_detail assumes a nonempty slice. Fast path folds monotonic comparisons and checks first>=0 plus final offset convertible to usize and within payload. Failure path reports first decreasing pair, then negative/unrepresentable value, then out-of-bounds value with position_base-adjusted indices. An unrepresentable positive offset would share the negative-offset message.

into_arrow_checked maps Arrow builder errors to contextual CorruptFile. The sole production unsafe block calls build_unchecked only after receiving the private proof; it avoids repeated offset/UTF-8 scans. into_arrow_builder moves full original buffers, sets requested datatype/count/null_count0 and preserves no separate bits_per_offset metadata. Safety depends on the matching prior validation and source platform assumptions.

Variable serialization orders offsets before payload. Public offsets_as_block takes mutable self but only clones offsets, sets fixed width/count+1 and new stats; it does not mutate the block. data_size adds the two visible lengths; count+1 and byte sums are ordinary arithmetic.

Public StructDataBlock exposes children, stats and optional NullBuffer. into_arrow requires Struct or returns Internal, zips fields with children, converts each child and assigns row count from the last visited child. Extra children are ignored; no children yields zero rows. Validity extraction takes the underlying buffer and null count without explicitly preserving a BooleanBuffer bit offset. Checked Arrow build validates resulting layout, but this file has no dedicated sliced-parent-validity regression.

Struct remove_outer_validity recursively transforms children and clears parent validity while retaining stats. Serialization flattens child buffers and omits parent validity. has_variable_width_child merely tests whether any direct child is not FixedWidth, counting FSL, Nullable and AllNull too. data_size likewise omits parent validity and stats.

Public DictionaryDataBlock exposes fixed-width indices and boxed dictionary. decode_helper returns AllNull0 for zero declared indices. Otherwise it estimates expanded capacity from dictionary byte size and counts with unchecked arithmetic, including division by dictionary count. It iterates all physically stored indices, not only declared num_values, converting keys to usize and appending one dictionary range each. Empty dictionaries or malformed keys can panic/error; no local normalization occurs.

Public decode interprets keys as unsigned native8/16/32/64 by physical width; unsupported width returns Internal. Requested Arrow Dictionary conversion compares physical index width with requested key byte width and reports CorruptFile on mismatch, then checked-converts keys and dictionary values and attaches the child with checked Arrow construction. Signed key interpretation is delegated to requested Arrow type rather than unsigned expansion.

Dictionary into_arrow dispatches declared Dictionary types to dictionary reconstruction; other requested types eagerly expand then convert. Buffer order is indices followed by dictionary buffers. Public into_parts returns DataBlock::FixedWidth indices plus unboxed dictionary; from_parts simply stores supplied components with no validation.

Public DataBlock has ten variants: Empty, Constant, AllNull, Nullable, FixedWidth, FixedSizeList, VariableWidth, Opaque, Struct, Dictionary. Docs describe zero-copy reconstruction but Boolean repacking and dictionary expansion allocate; Arrow-to-block normalization can also copy. Enum itself is Debug/Clone.

Public DataBlock::into_arrow ignores caller validate and dispatches with true. Empty produces Arrow empty array, Constant reaches todo, Opaque returns Internal requiring decoding first. Composite conversions recursively enforce their local checks; not every malformed public-field state yields a Result error.

into_buffers consumes each variant and flattens it in variant-specific order; Opaque returns its vector. There is no framing, type, count or version metadata in this operation. Struct parent validity omission means this is not a generic lossless Arrow serialization API.

try_clone returns Ok for every variant using derived/shared clones. Docs referring to borrowed-versus-owned modes, mutable self and borrow_and_clone are stale: signature is &self and current LanceBuffer wraps an Arrow Buffer. Physical data and BlockInfo maps are shared, not deep copied. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:12-27)

name returns fixed diagnostic variant strings. is_variable recurses through Nullable, FSL and Struct children; FixedWidth/Empty/AllNull/Constant are false. Dictionary is todo and Opaque panics. This method is distinct from Struct has_variable_width_child direct-kind test.

is_nullable returns true for AllNull/Nullable and recursively examines FSL/Struct children, but ignores Struct.validity. Dictionary is todo and Opaque panics. Thus it is not a complete logical Arrow nullability predicate.

num_values reads variant counts, delegates Nullable/FSL, takes Struct.children[0] without checking emptiness or agreement, and takes dictionary index count. The comment saying no recursion should not be read literally: Nullable/FSL recurse. Empty returns0.

items_per_row delegates Nullable, multiplies FSL dimension by child value, and returns1 for FixedWidth/VariableWidth/Dictionary/Opaque. Empty, Constant, AllNull and Struct remain todo panics. Products are unchecked.

data_size returns zero for Empty/AllNull, stored scalar size for Constant, visible physical bytes for leaves/composites and indices plus dictionary for Dictionary. Struct validity is omitted. Shared buffers can be counted repeatedly; this is not retained capacity or logical expanded size.

remove_outer_validity panics for AllNull, unwraps one Nullable layer, recursively clears Struct children/validity, and leaves other variants including FSL and Dictionary unchanged. Removing validity can expose arbitrary bytes under null slots. The recurse parameter described in docs does not exist.

make_builder chooses packed bitmap for fixed bits1, byte-aligned fixed builder otherwise, variable i32/i64, recursively FSL/Nullable/Struct, or AllNull. Nullable assigns estimated_bytes/16 to validity and the remainder to child; Struct divides estimate among children (zero for empty). Empty/Constant/Opaque/Dictionary and unsupported offset widths are todo; non-byte-aligned fixed widths panic. This method does not copy input values.

Three private macros generate consuming, shared-reference and mutable-reference Option casts using exact enum matching. They perform no nested unwrap, validation, conversion or statistic invalidation. Consuming wrong-variant casts return None and drop the consumed input.

Public DataBlock cast implementation invokes each macro for seven variants AllNull, Nullable, FixedWidth, FixedSizeList, VariableWidth, Struct and Dictionary, creating21 exact public methods. Empty, Constant and Opaque have no generated casts. Mutable casts allow mutation without refreshing shared stats.

Private get_byte_range<T> borrows typed offsets, returns0..0 for empty, otherwise casts first and last offsets to usize without validating sign, monotonicity or payload bounds. Mutable parameter does not imply mutation.

stitch_offsets<T> returns empty outputs for no buffers. Otherwise it reserves typed-element capacity using the sum of input byte lengths, inserts a leading zero, rebases each nonempty input by x+last_offset-start, and records original payload spans. Even one input is copied to normalize a nonzero start. Arithmetic adds before subtracting, so intermediate overflow is possible even when the rebased result would fit. Empty buffers contribute0..0 spans.

arrow_binary_to_data_block slices each ArrayData offset buffer using its element offset and len+1, stitches i32 for32-bit or i64 otherwise, slices corresponding payload ranges and copies concatenated payloads. It creates VariableWidth with caller-supplied count and empty stats. These operations assume valid inputs and do not independently verify total count.

encode_flat_data derives byte width from the first array type, reserves declared count*width and copies each ArrayData first buffer. There is no explicit ArrayData element-offset adjustment here; it relies on array to_data buffer representation. Sliced UInt16 tests cover one concrete case. Counts/types are not reconciled.

encode_bitmap_data obtains BooleanBuffer views and appends them to a new builder, preserving bit slicing through Arrow buffer APIs. Declared count controls initial capacity, not an enforced output bound. Output is a packed buffer.

concat_dict_arrays uses Arrow concat; DictionaryKeyOverflow triggers casting all inputs to UInt32 dictionary keys and retrying concat. A second key overflow is unimplemented beyond2^32 entries; other errors unwrap. It assumes nonempty dictionary arrays and matching usable types. Arrow concat controls merge/remap behavior; this code does not deduplicate values itself.
max_index_val maps eight signed/unsigned integer key types to their positive native maxima; other types panic. The result guides null-item insertion and index widening.

arrow_dictionary_to_data_block first concatenates dictionaries and derives actual key count. If logical validity exists, it reuses the first null dictionary item or appends a null item. A null-item index beyond current key maximum widens keys to UInt32; inability beyond that limit is unimplemented. This can happen with either a new or existing null dictionary item.

For nullable dictionaries, conversion encodes the null index in the chosen key type, copies key bytes and replaces every logically invalid row key. Validity is moved into the dictionary items; the fixed indices carry no validity bitmap. Without logical validity it clones key bytes. Dictionary items recursively convert through DataBlock::from, and key stats start empty.

Private Nullability distinguishes None, All and Some(NullBuffer). to_option clones only Some; it returns None for both no-nulls and all-null cases because the latter is handled by an earlier representation shortcut.

extract_nulls calls logical_nulls on every array, which can materialize dictionary logical validity. If none returns a bitmap it yields None; otherwise it concatenates bitmaps, filling missing ones with true. It classifies All by comparing null count with caller-supplied num_values, not summed actual lengths. A present all-valid bitmap can remain Some.

validate_variable_width_offsets<T> permits a zero-length array with an empty offset buffer, otherwise slices the selected offset span respecting ArrayData.offset and checks monotonicity/payload bounds. Arithmetic is unchecked but this helper is invoked after Arrow basic layout validation. It does not validate UTF-8.

validate_variable_width_layouts applies classic binary/string offset checks using i32/i64 and visits all child ArrayData. It intentionally avoids rescanning UTF-8 content; view-specific offsets are not handled by these custom branches. Basic Arrow validation remains separate.

validate_array_data first calls ArrayData.validate, then recursive offset checks, mapping errors to InvalidInput with field name and buffered-array index. Crate-internal validate_arrays runs this over every input; empty input succeeds. Public from_arrays does not invoke it. Both current structural and legacy primitive flush sites call it separately. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7575-7587; rust/lance-encoding/src/array_encoding/logical/primitive.rs:511-514)

Public infallible from_arrays returns AllNull0 when arrays is empty or declared count is0 before inspecting nonempty input type/nulls. It uses only first datatype, computes logical nullability and returns AllNull with declared count for all-null input. Classic Binary/Utf8 use32-bit normalization, Large variants64; BinaryView/Utf8View cast to classic32-bit with expect. Boolean uses packed fixed-width1.

Fixed-size binary, integer/unsigned, floats16/32/64, dates, times, timestamps, intervals, durations and decimals32/64/128/256 use raw fixed-width copy. Null yields AllNull. Dictionary uses key/null normalization. Declared count and actual copied lengths can disagree for misuse of this public infallible API.

Struct conversion collects each positional child across all input arrays and recursively converts using declared row count. It stores parent validity on StructDataBlock. Generic wrapping later also creates Nullable for Some, so a partially nullable Struct can retain parent validity in both inner and outer representations. Child type/shape agreement is assumed.

FixedSizeList conversion collects child values, recursively converts declared_count*dimension and wraps dimension cast to u64. List/LargeList/ListView/LargeListView/Map/RunEndEncoded/Union are unsupported panics unless zero/all-null shortcuts already returned. Unsupported logical type does not imply every invocation panics.

from_arrays computes statistics on the encoded inner representation, then wraps Some validity in Nullable with a fresh empty outer BlockInfo. Dictionaries skip this wrapper because nulls were normalized into items. Statistics may recurse into children or require existing child stats; Struct stats sum child MaxLength and can panic when a child lacks it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:56-71; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:579-597)

Public generic from_array uses the array actual len and wraps it in Arc before from_arrays. From<ArrayRef> likewise derives actual count. These wrappers avoid a caller-supplied count mismatch but preserve unsupported-type and downstream panics.

Private Debug DataBlockBuilderImpl defines validate_append, append_validated and consuming finish. Default append validates then mutates. It is not declared Send or Sync; full operation transactionality is not guaranteed by this two-step protocol.

Public Debug DataBlockBuilder holds estimated capacity and optional boxed implementation. with_capacity_estimate allocates no specific builder. First append/get_builder fixes shape using the input make_builder, and even a failed first append can leave that implementation installed. Public append delegates validation/mutation without an outer rollback.

Private append_ranges validates the complete source block once, then validates each range order/end before appending it. Later invalid ranges or append failures retain earlier appended ranges; it is not atomic. Public finish panics if no input ever initialized the builder. A zero-length append can initialize an empty result.

Test module imports Arrow builders/dictionary/list/string types, seeded RNG and rstest. Tests are local source evidence and were not executed in this goal. Fixtures construct both valid arrays and intentionally invalid ArrayData via unsafe build_unchecked.
Sliced UInt16 regression checks logical count4 and8 data bytes; it does not compare the numeric values. Nullable sliced UInt16 checks count3,6 data bytes and packed validity0b10.

String concatenation verifies combined logical count, validity0x1d, offsets[0,5,5,10,11,12,12,12] and payload helloworldab across null/empty values. Non-null case verifies abcdef with offsets[0,1,3,6].
StringView tests repeat exact null/empty concatenation expectations after conversion to classic32-bit offsets, including payload, count and validity.
BinaryView fixture foo/null/bar asserts normalized variable payload foobar after unwrapping nullable; it does not assert every offset or validity byte.
String-slice helper verifies count, offsets and payload for world, hello, helloworld and hellofoo from differently sliced chunks. This tests rebasing from nonzero offsets and concatenation.
Two rstest cases Utf8/LargeUtf8 construct ArrayData with element offset1, length1 and offsets[0,5,10], then validate and normalize to world with rebased[0,5].

Two invalid string-offset cases build malformed Utf8/LargeUtf8 ArrayData unsafely with a negative offset and require pre-encoding InvalidInput including the field name and an offset at index1 with value-1. They exercise validation before normalizing buffers.
LargeBinary hello/world verifies64-bit offsets[0,5,10], payload helloworld and logical count2.

Dictionary concatenation regression verifies keys[0,0,1,2,3] and dictionary payload abbc with four items from two inputs. Duplicate b dictionary values remain: this fixture does not promise global deduplication.
Dictionary null normalization tests null keys and preexisting null dictionary items. Both require keys[3,0,1,2,3], four dictionary items, bitmap0b111, offsets[0,1,2,3,3] and payload abc.

Despite cannot_add_null name, this regression verifies successful UInt8-to-UInt32 key widening for256 distinct strings plus null. It checks257 dictionary items, keys0..256, null index256 and32640 payload bytes.
All-null test covers UInt32, FixedSizeBinary2, List<UInt32> and Struct<UInt32>, ten values each, comparing roundtrip against Arrow new_null_array. Unsupported non-null List conversion is bypassed.
Despite cannot_concatenate name, dictionary concat test expects widening to UInt32 for two256-entry dictionaries, sequential keys0..511 and65536 payload bytes.

Seeded fixed-int data_size cases cover3 and400 rows with no nulls and two null patterns; expected visible value bytes plus ceiling-packed validity are compared. Three3-row arrays are also compared to Arrow concat size behavior. This is byte-accounting coverage, not allocation-capacity measurement.
Malformed variable block has a final offset100000 against14 payload bytes alphabetagamma; direct conversion must return contextual CorruptFile.
Four-byte fixed block declaring two Int32 values must error both through FixedWidth and DataBlock conversions for validate=false and true. Assertions check errors, not their variants/messages.
Three variable-builder cases cover decreasing i32/i64 offsets and an i32 out-of-bounds end. append must return CorruptFile with expected diagnostic fragment; no mutation rollback assertion is made.

Eleven malformed-layout cases span four classic types with bounds errors, negative/decreasing/interior-bad/short offsets, invalid Utf8 and LargeUtf8 payloads and an offset splitting a UTF-8 character. Both validation flag values must yield CorruptFile. The comment suggesting the flag chooses extra checks is stale: these paths ignore it.
Dictionary conversion with malformed variable-width values must reject them as CorruptFile even with validate=false. This covers nested variable validation.

Dictionary test rejects32-bit physical indices when requested key type is Int8 and asserts the width diagnostic. Key128 is also invalid for the three values, but width validation is encountered first.

Four valid classic Binary/LargeBinary/Utf8/LargeUtf8 cases include empty values and Unicode string content and require exact roundtrips under both flag values. Missing local tests include shared-cache mutation, empty Struct, parent validity in builders, FSL dimension mismatch, zero-width/bitmap misuse, extra dictionary indices, count disagreement, appended-range partial failure and padded/nonzero-base layouts.
